title: throughput_benchmark sample crashes with ld.so DFS assertion failure
signature: Inconsistency detected by ld.so dl-sort-maps Assertion maps_head maps failed|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Samples / Samples
failed_jobs.symptom: Test_throughput_benchmark_py.test failed: ld.so assertion in dl_sort_maps_dfs

key_errors: ERROR root:samples_common_test_class.py:312 Inconsistency detected by ld.so: dl-sort-maps.c: 272: _dl_sort_maps_dfs: Assertion `maps_head == maps' failed!
root_cause: The throughput_benchmark Python sample crashed with a dynamic linker (ld.so) assertion failure during DFS sort of shared library maps. This is an Infrastructure-level transient issue: it indicates shared library loading inconsistency in the runner environment, likely triggered by concurrent or multi-threaded loading of OpenVINO shared libraries, a race condition in the dynamic linker, or a corrupted/incompatible runner state. This is not caused by the PR code changes themselves. 189 other tests passed successfully.
reproduction_steps: N/A — runner-environment glibc/ld.so transient issue, not reproducible deterministically.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed job — this is a transient ld.so assertion that typically clears on retry.
If the failure recurs repeatedly on ARM64 runners, investigate whether TBB or other multi-threaded libraries in the build are triggering ld.so map sorting races.
Consider pinning or upgrading the runner's glibc version if this becomes persistent.
prevention_strategies: Monitor ld.so assertion frequency on ARM64 runners. If pattern recurs, file a runner infrastructure ticket. Consider using LD_PRELOAD or ld.so configuration to stabilize shared library loading order.
historical_context: No prior occurrences of this exact signature in the investigation database.
